summary: Over a 14-day analysis period, glycemic control is characterized by an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL, 86.0% time in range, 8.9% time above range, and 5.1% time below range. While daytime management maintains acceptable overall stability, late-night and early-morning dips below 70 mg/dL occur due to overly aggressive overnight basal segments, while afternoon and evening hyperglycemia spikes (150–160+ mg/dL) stem from unannounced meals compounded by GLP-1 therapy slowing gastric emptying.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is 98.7% with 3,995 valid entries and no duplicate or invalid records. Telemetry and device statuses are complete.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid CGM entries, 6214 device statuses, 2315 treatment entries across 14 days.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Structured carb entries are absent (0 g logged), indicating meals are recorded via notes or unparsed entries.

analysis_steps.findings: Time in range is 86.0%, but time below range reaches 5.1% with lows down to 41–42 mg/dL, primarily between local 01:00 and 06:00.
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, SD 39.7 mg/dL, CV 32.6%, TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates (0.6 to 0.8 U/h) drive early morning lows, whereas afternoon hours exhibit upward glucose drift.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local averages show dips to ~90 mg/dL overnight and peaks of 153–162 mg/dL in afternoon hours.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Basal effects overlap with active dynamic ISF scaling and unannounced meals.

analysis_steps.findings: Flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U combined with dynamic sensitivity (70% adjustment factor) and 10-hour DIA provides strong automated responsiveness but risks stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: ISF segments show a static 56 mg/dL/U; dynamic sensitivity active; DIA set to 10 hours.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of structured carb entries limits precise standalone ISF/CR verification.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled with smb_always_enabled=true, causing aggressive micro-bolusing during unannounced glucose rises.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS profile settings show smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic sensitivity scales down effectively during spikes, but max IOB of 25 U is overly wide relative to total daily dose.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true, max_iob_units=25 U, max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h.

analysis_steps.findings: Absence of structured carb entries forces reliance on UAM and reactive SMB dosing, leading to afternoon postprandial peaks.
analysis_steps.evidence: Total carbs 0.0g in summary; therapy response windows show variable correction outcomes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact meal timing and carbohydrate quantities are unparsed in structured logs.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb absorption max hours set to 7 hours, aligning with noted GLP-1 therapy (1.25mg) which delays gastric emptying.
analysis_steps.evidence: meal_max_absorption_hours=7h; representative events show GLP-1 1.25mg notes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No explicit e-carb entries recorded to evaluate custom duration offsets.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates require slight reduction to prevent hypoglycemic dips, while daytime automated loop settings and GLP-1 absorption dynamics benefit from structured meal logging rather than raw parameter changes.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined telemetry showing 5.1% TBR overnight and afternoon peaks.

strengths: High CGM data quality with 98.7% coverage over 14 days.
Strong overall time in range of 86.0%.
Effective closed-loop automation via AAPS with active dynamic sensitivity scaling.
issues: Overnight time below range reaches 5.1% with glucose dipping below 70 mg/dL due to slightly excessive early morning basal rates.
Afternoon and evening hyperglycemia peaks (150–160+ mg/dL) driven by unannounced meals and delayed gastric emptying under GLP-1 therapy.
Absence of structured carbohydrate entries forces the automated loop to rely entirely on UAM and reactive SMB dosing.

recommendations.title: Reduce Overnight Basal Rate
recommendations.description: Overnight and early morning glucose values show frequent dips below 70 mg/dL (up to 18.5% time below range at local hour 1), indicating that the 0.6–0.8 U/h basal segments are slightly too high during fasting.

recommendations.title: Review Max IOB Safety Limit
recommendations.description: The current max IOB limit of 25 U is exceptionally wide relative to total daily insulin needs, presenting a stacking risk if aggressive UAM triggers coincide with manual corrections.

recommendations.title: Establish Structured Carb Logging
recommendations.description: Total logged carbs are 0g, causing the system to rely solely on reactive UAM. Introducing consistent carb entry will allow AAPS to utilize CR and proper absorption timing.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight data shows consistent dips below 70 mg/dL during early morning hours (local 01:00–06:00), indicating that the midnight basal segment (0.6 U/h) is slightly too aggressive during fasting.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose for 5 to 7 days after adjusting the 00:00 basal segment to ensure time below range decreases without triggering rebound morning highs.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Safely adjust the midnight basal segment from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h while keeping all other profile and automation settings stable.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight glucose dips below 70 mg/dL in early morning hours; reducing baseline overnight delivery mitigates nocturnal hypoglycemia risk.
Current setting is adequate; verify stability after making the initial midnight basal adjustment.
Current setting provides necessary morning resistance coverage; keep unchanged pending sequential review.
Midday stability is acceptable; do not change multiple parameters simultaneously.
Afternoon peaks are driven by unannounced meals and GLP-1 absorption rather than basal deficits.
Maintains evening stability alongside dynamic ISF scaling.
Adequate coverage for evening transition hours.
Carb entries are unparsed in structured logs; maintain current CR until structured meal logging is established.
No evidence supporting a carb ratio change at this time.
Morning CR functions adequately with dynamic sensitivity.
Afternoon spikes relate to unannounced intake rather than ratio defects.
Evening ratio maintains stable post-dinner control when meals are covered.
Flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U works effectively in tandem with dynamic sensitivity (70%); changing static ISF prematurely risks over-correction.
Target is clinically appropriate for closed-loop operation.
Daytime target provides a safe buffer against activity-induced lows.
Maintains consistent overnight target matching.
A 10-hour DIA supports prolonged insulin action under closed-loop control, especially given GLP-1 slowed digestion.
Core automation features are functioning as intended to manage glucose dynamics.
Activation conditions appropriately support unannounced meal detection and micro-bolusing.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivery timing and limits are well-configured for closed-loop responsiveness.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Reducing max IOB from 25 U to 15 U improves safety against insulin stacking while remaining fully sufficient for normal automated delivery.
Dynamic sensitivity scaling (70%) properly compensates for postprandial volatility without needing static ISF alterations.
The 7-hour absorption model appropriately accommodates delayed gastric emptying associated with GLP-1 therapy.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Transition from unannounced meal reliance to proactive meal and carbohydrate logging with modest pre-boluses, allowing AAPS to dose smoothly over the 7-hour absorption window and account for GLP-1 delayed digestion.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Structured carb logging is absent (0g logged), causing afternoon hyperglycemia as the loop reacts via UAM/SMBs only after glucose rises.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record consistent carbohydrate amounts for meals over a 7-day period to evaluate whether proactive CR-based bolusing flattens the afternoon peak.

exceptions.suggestion: Maintain automated delivery while monitoring for nocturnal dips below 70 mg/dL.
exceptions.rationale: Early morning lows stem from overly aggressive basal rates rather than meal handling.

exceptions.pattern: Afternoon GLP-1 / Unannounced Intake Peaks (14:00–18:00 local)
exceptions.suggestion: Introduce structured meal announcements to avoid delayed upward drift.
exceptions.rationale: Prevents reliance on reactive UAM micro-boluses under slowed gastric emptying.

implementation_steps: Verify current CGM and pump telemetry stability before making any adjustments.
Implement the overnight basal change (00:00 basal to 0.5 U/h) and monitor overnight glucose for 5 to 7 days.
Review max IOB settings and consider tightening to 15 U to reduce insulin stacking risk.
Begin recording structured meal carbohydrate entries to evaluate proactive bolusing and improve automated loop response.
education: Closed-loop systems with SMB and UAM enabled rely heavily on accurate carbohydrate inputs; unannounced meals force the algorithm to react to glucose rises rather than preempting them.
GLP-1 receptor agonists slow gastric emptying, shifting carbohydrate absorption over a longer multi-hour window that benefits from extended absorption settings and proactive meal declarations.
